summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around defense subtier visibility and supply-chain resilience. The key pattern is that policy attention appears to be shifting from prime-contractor awards toward mapping lower-tier dependencies, compliant sourcing, and capacity at obscure material/component suppliers. This pass keeps one high-attention reference platform and three underfollowed or niche candidates with plausible direct exposure to subtier illumination, critical-material compliance, or qualified defense supply bottlenecks. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Expanded the node around defense subtier visibility into a two-lane universe: one high-attention reference platform for supply-chain illumination, and three underfollowed or speculative small/mid-cap candidates tied to scarce defense inputs, subtier components, and sustainment/logistics capacity. The strongest direct evidence in this pass is for UAMY as a regulated strategic-materials supplier with a sole-source DLA contract, and for PLTR as a reference software/data platform in naval industrial-base supply-chain workflows. DCO and VSEC are included as underfollowed hypotheses because their filings/company materials show aerospace-defense components or aftermarket/MRO supply-chain roles, but their exact leverage to DoD supply-chain illumination reforms requires contract-level verification.
